title: AWL Sublist 5
description: Quinta sublista de la Academic Word List: 60 familias para hablar de cambio, sociedad, ciencia y economía con precisión.

cards.definition: A school or college for special training; an official society of scholars.
cards.example: Academic performance is closely linked to sleep and diet.
cards.warning: 'Academia' (escuela privada de repaso/idiomas) se dice 'language school' o 'private tutoring centre'.

cards.definition: To change something slightly; to get used to a new situation.
cards.example: International students often need time to adjust to a new culture.
cards.warning: 'Adjust to + -ing': 'adjust to living abroad', no 'adjust to live'.

cards.definition: To change something, usually slightly.
cards.example: Climate change is altering the migration patterns of many birds.
cards.warning: 'Alterarse' (ponerse nervioso) es 'get upset', no 'alter'.

cards.definition: To make small changes to a law, document or text to improve it.
cards.example: The law was amended to protect online privacy.
cards.warning: 'Make amends' = compensar un daño; 'amend' = modificar un texto.

cards.definition: Knowing that something exists or is happening.
cards.example: Consumers are increasingly aware of the environmental cost of fast fashion.
cards.warning: Es 'aware of', no 'aware about'. 'Concienciar' = 'raise awareness'.

cards.definition: The amount something can contain or produce; the ability to do something.
cards.example: Many hospitals are operating at full capacity during the winter.

cards.definition: Something difficult that tests ability; to question whether something is right.
cards.example: The findings challenge the belief that money brings happiness.

cards.definition: A part of a sentence with a verb; a section of a legal document.
cards.example: The contract contains a clause that allows either side to withdraw.

cards.definition: A substance of two or more elements; to make a problem worse.
cards.example: The housing shortage was compounded by rising interest rates.

cards.definition: A serious disagreement or fight; to be very different or incompatible.
cards.example: There is often a conflict between economic growth and environmental protection.

cards.definition: To ask for advice or information from someone or a source.
cards.example: Residents were not consulted before the factory was built.
cards.warning: 'Consulta' médica (el lugar) es 'surgery' o 'doctor's office'.

cards.definition: Communication or meeting with someone; to communicate with someone.
cards.example: Children who have contact with animals may develop fewer allergies.
cards.warning: Como verbo no lleva preposición: 'contact the university', no 'contact with the university'.

cards.definition: A gradual decrease in amount or quality; to decrease; to refuse politely.
cards.example: The number of smokers declined steadily between 2000 and 2020.
cards.note: Verbo clave para IELTS Task 1: 'declined sharply/gradually'.

cards.definition: Clearly separate or different from others.
cards.example: The course is divided into three discrete units.
cards.warning: No confundir 'discrete' (separado) con 'discreet' (discreto, prudente), que suenan igual.

cards.definition: An early version of a text; to write a first version.
cards.example: Students should revise their first draft before submitting it.

cards.definition: To make it possible for someone to do something.
cards.example: Online banking enables customers to manage their money anywhere.
cards.warning: Estructura: 'enable someone to do', no 'enable to do' sin objeto ni 'enable doing'.

cards.definition: Power from electricity, fuel, etc.; the strength to be active.
cards.example: Renewable energy now provides a third of the country's electricity.

cards.definition: To make people obey a law or rule.
cards.example: Speed limits are difficult to enforce on rural roads.
cards.warning: 'Reforzar' es 'reinforce' o 'strengthen', no 'enforce'.

cards.definition: Something that exists separately and independently.
cards.example: The two companies continue to operate as separate legal entities.

cards.definition: Equal in value, amount or meaning to something else.
cards.example: The scheme costs the equivalent of £50 per household.

cards.definition: To develop gradually over time.
cards.example: The role of libraries has evolved in the digital age.

cards.definition: To become or make larger in size, number or importance.
cards.example: The university plans to expand its online programmes.
cards.note: 'Expand on an idea' = desarrollar una idea con más detalle (muy útil en Speaking).

cards.definition: To uncover something hidden; to put someone in contact with something.
cards.example: Children exposed to two languages early often become fluent in both.
cards.warning: 'Exponer' un trabajo en clase es 'present', no 'expose'.

cards.definition: Coming from or relating to the outside.
cards.example: Small economies are vulnerable to external shocks.

cards.definition: To make an action or process easier or more likely.
cards.example: Technology can facilitate communication between teachers and parents.
cards.warning: 'Facilitar' datos (dar) es 'provide', no 'facilitate data'. 'Facilities' = instalaciones.

cards.definition: Forming the basic or most important part of something.
cards.example: Access to education is a fundamental human right.

cards.definition: To produce or create something, such as energy, income or interest.
cards.example: Tourism generates around 10% of the country's income.

cards.definition: All the people born around the same time; the production of something.
cards.example: Younger generations are more comfortable with digital technology.

cards.definition: A picture; the way something or someone is seen by the public.
cards.example: The scandal damaged the company's public image.

cards.definition: Respecting different opinions; supporting individual freedom and gradual reform.
cards.example: Attitudes towards marriage have become more liberal.
cards.warning: En EE. UU. 'liberal' suele significar 'progresista' (izquierda), no 'liberal económico' como en España.

cards.definition: An official document giving permission to do or own something.
cards.example: Drivers must renew their licence every ten years.
cards.note: Británico: licence (sustantivo), license (verbo). Americano: license para ambos.

cards.definition: A way of thinking based on sensible reasons; the science of reasoning.
cards.example: The logic behind the policy is that higher prices reduce demand.

cards.definition: The difference between amounts; the edge of a page or area.
cards.example: The proposal was approved by a narrow margin.

cards.definition: Relating to medicine and the treatment of illness.
cards.example: Advances in medical research have increased life expectancy.
cards.warning: 'El médico' (persona) es 'doctor' o 'physician', no 'a medical'.

cards.definition: Relating to the mind.
cards.example: Mental health problems are increasingly common among teenagers.

cards.definition: To change something slightly, usually to improve it.
cards.example: Genetically modified crops remain controversial in Europe.

cards.definition: To watch and check something over time; a screen.
cards.example: Scientists closely monitor air quality in major cities.
cards.warning: 'Monitor' de tiempo libre (persona) es 'instructor' o 'coach'.

cards.definition: A system of connected people, lines or computers; to meet people for work.
cards.example: A good public transport network reduces car dependence.

cards.definition: An idea or belief about something.
cards.example: The study challenges the notion that older workers are less productive.
cards.warning: 'Tener nociones de' (conocimientos básicos) es 'have a basic knowledge of', no 'have notions of'.

cards.definition: An aim; based on facts rather than personal feelings.
cards.example: Journalists should present information in an objective way.

cards.definition: To aim something at a particular group or purpose; to find your position.
cards.example: The course is oriented towards students with no prior experience.

cards.definition: A particular way of thinking about something; a point of view.
cards.example: From an economic perspective, the project makes sense.

cards.definition: Very accurate and exact.
cards.example: It is difficult to give a precise figure for unemployment.
cards.warning: 'Preciso' (necesario) es 'necessary'. 'Es preciso que' = 'It is necessary that'.

cards.definition: Main or most important; of the best quality.
cards.example: Unemployment is a prime cause of social unrest.

cards.definition: The scientific study of the mind and behaviour.
cards.example: Child psychology helps explain how young people learn.

cards.definition: To try to achieve something over time; to follow or chase.
cards.example: More women are choosing to pursue careers in engineering.

cards.definition: The relationship between two amounts, shown as two numbers.
cards.example: The ratio of students to teachers has risen to 30:1.
collocations: the ratio of X to Y

cards.definition: To refuse to accept, believe or consider something.
cards.example: Voters rejected the proposal by a large majority.

cards.definition: Income received by a government or company.
cards.example: Tax revenue from tobacco has fallen as fewer people smoke.

cards.definition: Firm and not likely to change or fail.
cards.example: The population of the city remained stable throughout the decade.

cards.definition: A particular way of doing something; a fashionable design.
cards.example: Different students have different learning styles.

cards.definition: A person or thing used instead of another; to use instead.
cards.example: Online lessons are not a perfect substitute for face-to-face teaching.
cards.warning: Ojo al orden: 'substitute A for B' = usar A en lugar de B. Más claro: 'replace B with A'.

cards.definition: To keep something going over time; to suffer an injury or loss.
cards.example: The current rate of economic growth cannot be sustained.

cards.definition: A sign or object that represents something else.
cards.example: The bicycle has become a symbol of sustainable urban life.

cards.definition: A goal to achieve; to aim at a particular group.
cards.example: The campaign targets young adults who rarely vote.
cards.warning: Como verbo no lleva preposición: 'target young people', no 'target to young people'.

cards.definition: The movement of people or goods from one place to another.
cards.example: Some goods were damaged in transit.
cards.warning: 'Tránsito' de coches (tráfico) es 'traffic'; 'public transit' (EE. UU.) = 'public transport' (UK).

cards.definition: A general direction in which something is changing.
cards.example: The graph shows an upward trend in online sales.

cards.definition: A form of something that is slightly different from other forms.
cards.example: An updated version of the report was published last year.

cards.definition: Health, comfort and happiness; government help for people in need.
cards.example: Animal welfare groups campaign against intensive farming.
cards.warning: En EE. UU. 'be on welfare' = vivir de ayudas sociales. 'Bienestar' personal suele ser 'well-being'.

cards.definition: Used to compare two facts and show a contrast between them.
cards.example: Car use rose in rural areas, whereas it fell in large cities.
cards.warning: 'Whereas' une dos oraciones contrastadas; no significa 'mientras' temporal (eso es 'while').
